figures.caption: Table 1. Decoding tasks. Trials per class are per participant. For ds003626 the inner-speech condition is the primary task and the pronounced condition is reported for comparison.

Table 2. Shuffle-label controls for the positive results reported in this paper. Accuracy is the value measured in this study. Labels were permuted within participant and the pipeline re-run 200 times, or 50 times for the network, whose every draw is a full retraining. No null draw reached the observed value in any row, so each empirical p equals its minimum of 1/(n+ 1): 0.005 for 200 draws and 0.020 for 50.

Table 3. Content decoding with the reference decoder. All values were measured in this study; accuracy is the mean over participants. “5-fold” pools sessions and is optimistic; “held out” tests on an unseen session (ds003626) or an unseen block of trials (other corpora). Chance is 0.200 for the five phrases, 0.250 for the four-word tasks and 0.143 for the seven phonemes. Threshold is the exact binomial per-participant threshold at α = 0.05; n≥ is the number of participants at or above it; p is the one-sided Wilcoxon test against chance; CI is the bootstrap 95% confidence interval.

Figure 1. Pairwise word separability by corpus, band and protocol. Each box summarizes one value per participant, that participant’s accuracy averaged over the corpus’s word pairs. The box spans the interquartile range, the center line is the median, the diamond is the mean, whiskers extend to 1.5 times the interquartile range and circles mark participants beyond them; fill and hatching identify the band. The dashed line is chance and the dotted segments each corpus’s per-participant threshold.

Table 4. Pairwise word separability on matched 128Hz, 1–45Hz data. Chance is 0.500. Mean accuracy is over pairs; the CI treats participants as the unit, averaging each participant over pairs first. FDR correction is within each corpus.

Figure 2. Every phrase pair of the competition corpus, within subject (top) and across participants (bottom), in four bands. Each box summarizes the 15 participants, drawn as in figure 1. The dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant threshold (0.569).

Table 5. Cross-subject decoding with subject-level alignment (LOSO, band power, 8–30Hz). Every alignment is fitted per participant from that participant’s unlabeled trials; “inductive K” uses only the first K trials. Per-participant thresholds are 0.235 (competition), 0.305 (ds003626) and 0.367 (KaraOne). Change is relative to no alignment.

Figure 3. Accuracy of decoders trained on one participant and tested on another (hatched bars, one value per ordered pair), against each participant’s within-subject accuracy (outlined bars). Both are plotted as proportions so that pairs and participants share an axis. The dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant threshold.

Figure 4. Within-subject accuracy of each participant against the mean accuracy of that participant’s decoder on every other participant. Each point is one participant; the dashed lines mark chance, and ρ is Spearman’s rank correlation.

Table 8. Rest, pre-imagery and imagery windows on KaraOne (LOSO, band power, re-referenced scalp channels). The pre-imagery interval lies between rest and imagery and contains perception of the prompt and preparation to articulate it. Above: each pair of windows decoded directly; threshold is the mean of the per-participant thresholds, and each participant is counted in n≥ against their own. Below: fraction of each window type that the rest-versus-imagery decoder, trained on the other participants, labelled as imagery. Each p is a one-sided Wilcoxon test across participants; the shuffle-label controls for the upper rows are in table 2.

Figure 5. Time-resolved decoding with 500ms windows in 50ms steps. Each point is the mean accuracy over participants in one window, with its 95% confidence interval; filled points belong to a cluster that survives the cluster-based permutation test over time. The solid line is the accuracy of the full analysis window, the dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant threshold.

Table 9. Phonological contrasts on KaraOne with the test prompts held out of training (112 valid hold-out combinations in total). “All” uses all 11 prompts; “phonemes” uses the seven phonemes only. q is corrected across the family.
